title: Identity guardrails: pricing experiment and contract commitments for SSO/SAML + RBAC
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We need a controlled pricing and contracting experiment to determine how contractual commitments for SSO/SAML and role-based access control (RBAC) affect conversion, expansion, and operational risk for Enterprise customers. The goal is to decide a repeatable packaging pattern and contract language that balances sales velocity, legal exposure, and security posture.

Background / problem:
Enterprise customers increasingly ask for explicit contractual commitments around identity — not just 'we support SAML' but obligations: timelines for SSO enablement, RBAC primitives in the console, audit log retention, and proof points for compliance reviews. Sales teams report friction when identity requirements are only treated as 'implementation work' and not reflected in pricing or SLAs. Legal and Security want clear boundaries for responsibilities (customer-managed IdP vs Redwood-managed assist).

Goals / success metrics (experiment):
- Primary: conversion rate lift on >$50k ARR deals when SSO/RBAC options are clearly priced and committed in contract terms (target +10% conversion within experiment cohort).
- Secondary: deal velocity (days to close), expansion lift (percentage of customers that upgrade to higher tiers for managed identity services), reduction in security review cycles (avg. review time).
- Safety metrics: legal escalations, post-deploy identity incidents, spike in implementation engineering requests.

Hypotheses:
1) Offering two clear identity packaging options (Standard enterprise: SSO + RBAC included at commit threshold; Managed Identity add-on: paid, SLA-backed enablement) will increase close rates by reducing ambiguity in procurement.
2) A modest one-time setup fee for Managed Identity reduces open engineering work and aligns expectations, producing net positive NPV.
3) Contractual commitments (time-to-enable SSO, audit log retention, breach-response obligations) will reduce back-and-forth with procurement teams and shorten legal review time.

Experiment design:
Cohorts (12-week running experiment):
- Cohort A (Control): Current approach — SSO/SAML and RBAC described in scope of work, no explicit commercial packaging or SLA in standard MSA.
- Cohort B (Packaged): Introduce two packaged options on quotes: "Enterprise Identity (included at commit X)" and "Managed Identity (one-time fee + monthly)". Both include standard contract language templates.
- Cohort C (Contract-first): For high-touch prospects (> $250k ARR) require a short identity appendix in the SOW that lists time-to-enable, role-mapping support, and audit log retention with a nominal SLA.
Assignment will be randomized by deal size and sales region, with Sales Ops instrumenting quoting templates.

Contract language variants to test (drafts attached in Links):
- Variant 1: Commitment-lite: Redwood will provide SSO/SAML and RBAC features; enablement timelines are 'commercially reasonable' and included as best-effort.
- Variant 2: SLA-enabled: Redwood commits to enablement within X business days post-signature, provides role-mapping primitives, and an audit log retention of Y days. Remedy limited to credits capped at setup fee.
- Variant 3: Shared-responsibility: Customer owns IdP configuration; Redwood provides documented enablement assistance; add-on Managed Identity available for turnkey integration with defined deliverables.

Engineering and Console scope: (dependencies listed above)
- Minimum viable RBAC controls: team/role creation, role assignment audit trail, API to sync groups (ENG-1842).
- SSO enablement UX: quote-to-console provisioning path, enablement checklist for SEs (ENG-2056, DES-3310).
- Billing hooks for one-time setup fees and monthly managed-identity charges (billing team feature).

Legal / Security review notes:
- Legal asks for clear limitation of liability on identity misconfiguration and definitions for 'enablement' (what counts as complete).
- Security requests that the contract reference KMS integration for key management where appropriate and preserve customer audit rights.
- We will bring two contract appendix templates to Sales and GC for sign-off.

Decision checkpoints:
- 2025-03-18: Draft contract appendix + experiment instrumentation ready (sign-off by Legal and Security).
- 2025-03-31: Begin cohort assignment and quoting templates updated.
- 2025-06-01: Early read of conversion metrics; adjust pricing or SLA caps.
- 2025-07-01: Final recommendation to leadership: default packaging + standard appendix OR require bespoke clauses for top tier deals.

Trade-offs discussed:
- Strict SLAs (fast enablement windows) improve sales but increase operational load and possible credit exposure. We propose remedy limited to capped credits tied to set-up fees to mitigate risk.
- Bundling identity into base Enterprise SKU improves simplicity but reduces ability to capture set-up revenue and may overload implementation teams.
- Making RBAC mandatory increases security posture but may slow adoption for smaller customers; consider commit thresholds (e.g., included above $100k ARR).

Operational runbook for Managed Identity (draft):
- SE opens identity intake ticket, ENGR Triage within 24h, implementation sprint within committed SLA, post-implementation handover and audit log sampling for 30 days.

Next steps / asks:
- Legal: finalize two appendix templates and confirm acceptable remedy language by 2025-03-14.
- Security: confirm required audit log retention defaults and minimal RBAC schema by 2025-03-14.
- Engineering: confirm feasibility of group-sync API and estimate points for RBAC primitives by 2025-03-07.
- Sales Enablement: update quote templates and playbook for experiment cohorts by 2025-03-25.

Artifacts and where to find them (Links):
- Confluence experiment brief: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/ID-IDENTITY-2025
- Draft contract appendix (Google Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/identity-contract-drafts
- Figma mockups for console RBAC: https://www.figma.com/file/identity-rbac-mockups
- GitHub epic and engineering PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls?q=identity
- Sales quote templates (internal): https://docs.google.com/document/d/quote-templates-identity

Evaluation plan / dashboards:
- Instrument GA events for quote type, appendix included, and whether Managed Identity was purchased.
- Dashboard (Looker): conversion_by_quote_type, avg_days_to_close, expansion_rate_post_90d, identity_related_eng_tickets_count.

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Engineering underestimates integration effort -> Mitigation: reserve buffer and offer managed-identity for complex IdPs.
- Risk: Legal changes requested late -> Mitigation: escalate and use temporary SOW addendum.
- Risk: Customers request custom identity integrations outside scope -> Mitigation: price as professional services.
